Verified date 2026-06-07.
    * One-fact summary: 4-row table — INNER/LEFT/RIGHT/FULL OUTER — which side keeps rows, what NULL-fill means, SaaS phrasing of each.
    * OUTER keyword optional (LEFT JOIN = LEFT OUTER JOIN); INNER = JOIN default.
    * NULL-fill explanation: row IS in result; left columns SELECTable; right columns just NULL.
    * Worked example with 3 users + 3 orders + 1 zero-match parent: INNER drops user_3; LEFT keeps user_3 NULL-padded; FULL OUTER adds orphan-order rows.
    * The COUNT(right_col) vs COUNT(*) pitfall: 3 phrasings × different answers (cnt_star=1 WRONG vs cnt_orderid=0 CORRECT vs cnt_explicit=0 CORRECT); the rule `COUNT(*)` counts ROWS, `COUNT(col)` skips NULL values; SUM is self-healing (skips NULL), AVG divides by non-NULL count.
    * 5-row DO-NOT-WRITE: (1) LEFT/INNER same rows just slower FALSE, (2) COUNT(*) after LEFT JOIN gives match count FALSE (gives row count incl NULL-padded), (3) COALESCE(COUNT(*), 0) fixes the zero-match case FALSE (COUNT(*) never returns NULL), (4) WHERE right.col IS NULL after LEFT JOIN = anti-join pattern (load-bearing distinction from INNER), (5) Moving LEFT JOIN's filter from ON to WHERE is equivalent FALSE — WHERE on right.col turns LEFT into INNER (classic silent-wrong trap) + the AND-in-ON workaround.
    * 4-step decision rule: identify must-keep side; put must-keep on LEFT; use LEFT JOIN (or FULL OUTER if both); use COUNT(<right_key>) not COUNT(*) for match counts; COALESCE(SUM(...), 0) only when downstream needs 0 instead of NULL.
    * Cross-refs: r07 §1a.2 (ARRAY_AGG-over-LEFT-JOIN-unmatched), §4 (calendar gap-fill LEFT JOIN), r23 §10 (anti-join LEFT JOIN ... WHERE right IS NULL), r23 §9 (JOIN ordering + ANALYZE for CBO).
